thread:
Maya R.: Heads-up — planning rollout strategy for the "surge-gate" tenant-prioritization feature (lets us degrade non-critical tenants under extreme spikes). Need agreement on gates, canary sizes, and rollback criteria. Thoughts?
Ashwin K.: +1 we should treat this as a multi-dim rollout: safety (latency/errors), business (top-tenants), and cost. suggest phased exposure with automatic backoff.
Julia P.: Agree. Minimal canary: 0.05% traffic from synthetic/seed tenants first, then 1%, 10%, 50%. Each step should have a 30m bake window and explicit metric checks.
Tom S.: What metrics exactly? p99 latency, 5xx rate, successful calls pct, and cost-per-1k-tokens delta. Also monitor SLO-alert count across regions.
Maya R.: Proposed gating thresholds: p99 <= +20% vs baseline, 5xx delta <= 0.1pp absolute, error budget consumption < 5% in bake window. If violated -> immediate rollback to previous flag state. OK?
Ashwin K.: Sounds good. Add user-visible regression guard: feature should not increase customer-facing failed requests (503s) more than 0.05pp for any paying tenant in the canary group.
Li Wei: Ops notes: need autoscale hook tested for sudden shedding. Also implement a fast kill switch in the console and an API call like: 
```
POST /flags/surge_gate/override
{ "state": "off", "reason": "trace-id-..." }
```
rollout-bot: Added task to rollout board: SURGE-GATE-2026. Assigned to @Maya R., @Li Wei. Canaries: 0.05% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%. Bake: 30m per step. Rollback auto-thresholds set.
Julia P.: We should run an A/B variant for 2 weeks against 5k daily active sessions to measure UX regressions (latency vs control). Use 10% of eligible tenants for A/B, seeded by tenant tier.
Tom S.: For tenant prioritization, include per-tenant SLA guards: do not apply to paid-tier tenants unless explicit opt-in. Add whitelist of top-50 tenants excluded by default.
Maya R.: Launch criteria checklist (draft):
- Canary success across 3 regions
- No new perf regressions (per thresholds)
- Runbook and kill-switch verified
- CSM/customer comms drafted for top affected tenants
- Post-launch telemetry dashboard and alerting
- A/B results within acceptable bounds
Anyone add to this?
Ashwin K.: Add: rollback runbook walkthrough completed with oncall and SRE, and a simulated failover test (flip flag + load spike) in staging.
Li Wei: I'll own the staged failover test and autoscale verification. Also will add alert tags: "surge_gate" to make paging obvious.
Julia P.: On scope negotiation: initial launch should only support two policies (soft-shed, hard-shed). Defer per-tenant custom policies to post-launch iteration.
Tom S.: For customer-driven asks: CSMs already flagged 3 enterprise customers who want explicit opt-in controls. We'll surface that as a follow-up epic and not block launch.
Maya R.: Great. Next steps: I'll update the rollout doc and feature flag config, schedule the staged failover test with @Li Wei, and we can start the 0.05% canary next week. Thanks all :thumbsup:
rollout-bot: Reminder — please add your signoffs in the rollout doc: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/SURGE-GATE-2026
(automated reminder in 24h)
